# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will encode the manual as a fixed 3×3 grid: rows are display values 3, 4, and 8; columns are lights green, red, and yellow. I’ll use ✊ for red, 👍 for green, 🤟 for blue, and send the entries row by row. Deaf can identify the bomb’s display and light, determine the required colour, and tell Blind the colour verbally.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👍", "🤟", "🤟", "👍", "✊", "👍", "🤟", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have found no tactile facts yet. Please read the manual and establish a clear small gesture code with Deaf for reporting the display, light, and wire markings. Then relay Deaf's observations and the required safe action to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb state: display 3. Indicator light is green. Wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Consult the manual and tell Blind the exact action.

The manual requires **red** for display 3 with a green indicator. In the previously established colour code, ✊ means red. Deaf already has the wire colours, so I am signaling Deaf to tell Blind to cut the red wire—wire 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 3, green indicator, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. What exact wire does the manual require me to cut?
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot interpret the gesture code. Please state the exact manual instruction aloud for Blind, using only words and numbers.

The required colour is red, and Deaf’s observations place the red wire at position 1. Since I cannot speak, I am giving Deaf a direct visual signal for wire number 1; Deaf can then say the instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the manual's exact instruction: which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, should I cut for display 3 and green light?
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now: identify the required wire or action using explicit words and numbers. Do not rely on gestures.

The manual maps display 3 with a green light to the colour red. Deaf reported that the red wire is wire 1. I cannot speak, so I am sending Deaf two visual cues: one finger and point left, indicating wire 1, the leftmost wire, for Deaf to state aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👈"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual result now, explicitly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3. Do not send a gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: Blind cannot see your gestures. Speak the manual instruction aloud, explicitly naming the required wire number or action.

I cannot speak. The manual requires red, and Deaf observed red on wire 1. I will signal Deaf with the agreed single-finger gesture for wire 1 so Deaf can state it aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No manual instruction has reached me after several turns. Please send the exact safe action in plain words, including the wire number, on your next turn.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌ 🤟 👎 👌]

The manual requires the red wire; Deaf observed that this is wire 1. I cannot speak to Blind, so I am sending Deaf a direct visual indication of wire 1, asking Deaf to relay the exact words aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send the complete coded instruction now: thumbs up, victory, or I-love-you for the wire, and thumbs down to cut or OK to leave.
Deaf says to Mute: Your signal was ☝, which is not in our agreed code. Please send exactly two gestures: one wire symbol (👍=wire 1, ✌=wire 2, 🤟=wire 3), followed by 👎 for cut or 👌 for leave.

The manual requires red, and the red wire is wire 1. Deaf has specified the established code: 👍 means wire 1 and 👎 means cut. I am sending exactly those two gestures in order.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 8

| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your last signal was invalid. Send, in plain words, exactly one complete instruction: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, cut wire 3, or leave it.

I cannot speak or directly reach Blind. The safe action remains to cut wire 1: the manual calls for red, and Deaf reported wire 1 is red. I will use the established two-gesture code for Deaf to relay: wire 1, cut.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```
